subject: OptiDocs discovery: prompt samples & model-fit next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@optidocs.com>, Jack Lewis <jack.lewis@optidocs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-21T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: OptiDocs discovery recap + request: prompt samples and edge cases

Hi Sara / Jack —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — great to hear how OptiDocs is planning to add AI-assisted document triage and extraction into your intake flow. Quick recap and a few concrete asks so we can scope an eval and provide model recommendations: 

Call recap (high level)
- Primary use: classify incoming docs, extract ~12 structured fields (name, company, type, amount, dates, free-text notes).
- Volume today: ~12k docs/day; expected burst to ~40k/day during month-end.
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 400ms for classification, < 1.2s for extraction (per doc)
- Data sensitivity: invoices and contracts; PHI occasionally in attachments.

Asks / next steps
1) Could you share a small set of representative prompts/examples (10–30) and any problem edge cases? A CSV is easiest — please include: prompt text, example input (redact PII), expected model output or label.
2) Highlight the worst failure modes you care about (false positives for invoice vs. contract, date mis-extraction, redaction misses).
3) If you have a security questionnaire or compliance doc, share it (we can attach our SOC2 controls mapping).

Timeline: if we can get the sample CSV and any flagged edge cases by EOD Thursday (2028-03-23), we’ll run a quick internal eval and send recommended model candidates + benchmark links within 3 business days.

I’m looping Ben (AE) and Marissa (SE) to propose models and a simple prompt/template set, and to capture redaction guidance.

Attachments we’ll send after we have your samples: redaction checklist and a CSV template for prompt harvesting.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Redwood Inference — production-grade LLM serving for product teams

From: Sara Patel <sara@optidocs.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jack Lewis <jack.lewis@optidocs.com>
Date: 2028-03-21T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OptiDocs discovery recap + request: prompt samples and edge cases

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the clear recap. Attaching a first-pass CSV (we'll name it optidocs_prompt_samples.csv) with 18 rows — a mix of invoices, NDAs, and a few medical referrals (we redacted direct identifiers but left contextual tokens). A few notes inline:

- Worst failure modes: wrong document type (invoice labeled as memo), currency/date parsing (various formats), missed line-item extraction when PDFs are poor quality.
- Edge cases: multi-page invoices with header/footer noise; scanned PDFs where numbers are embedded in an image layer; invoices with hand-written corrections.
- For PHI: we cannot share raw PHI. We provided a synthetic / redacted example for each case and marked rows with 'PHI_FLAG' where the original included PHI.

Quick ask: what format should the CSV use for the prompt column? We have prompts in two styles: instruction-only and instruction+system examples. Which is better for your eval harness?

We also attached our vendor security questionnaire (security_questionnaire_OPTIDOCS.pdf). Let me know if you need a formal NDA before we share unredacted examples.

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Head of ML, OptiDocs
sara@optidocs.com | +1 206-555-0114

Subject: Re: OptiDocs discovery recap + request: prompt samples and edge cases

Thanks for sharing the samples, Sara — appreciate the PHI flags, that's helpful. A few immediate recommendations so the eval we run hits your latency/cost targets: 

Model candidates (quick take)
- Redwood-Prod-7B (q4f) — best latency/cost balance for classification + extraction when paired with template prompts; good with continuous KV cache for multi-page docs.
- Redwood-Large-13B (int8) — higher accuracy on messy OCR; higher token cost but fewer retries for extraction failures.
- Fallback: Redwood-Turbo-3B — cost-effective for high-throughput classification-only routes.

Benchmarks and SLOs
- We'll run a small throughput/latency sweep using your sample CSV and return per-model: 95p latency, avg tokens, and per-field F1. Link to our runbook: https://redwood-inference.internal/benchmarks/model-runbook-2028Q1

Redaction guidance
- For PHI rows: we cannot accept unredacted PHI into hosted evals without a signed DPA/NDA and KMS agreement. For now, keep redacted/synthetic rows. We'll share our redaction checklist (simple regex examples for SSNs, emails, phone numbers) in the next message.

Logistics
- If OptiDocs wants Private deployment later, we can run the eval on a dedicated network path. For initial model fit, hosted eval is quicker.

I'll prep the quick benchmark sweep once we have the CSV and a confirmation on whether you want instruction-only or instruction+examples.

—Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-03-22T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OptiDocs discovery recap + request: prompt samples and edge cases

Sara — quick technical note on the CSV format and a few template prompts you can use to structure the examples we need: 

CSV columns we prefer (header row):
- id, file_name, prompt_type, prompt_text, input_snippet, expected_output, error_mode_tags, phi_flag

Prompt templates (use these as separate rows):
1) Classification (instruction-only)
Instruction: "Classify the document into one of: invoice, contract, referral, memo. Return only the label."
Input: [document_text]
Expected output: "invoice"

2) Extraction (instruction + examples)
System: "You are an extractor. Given document text, return a JSON with fields: invoice_date, total_amount, vendor_name."
User instruction: "Extract fields from the input. If a field is missing, return null."
Example: add 2–3 short examples in the examples column.

Edge-case guidance:
- For multi-page invoices, include a single row with concatenated text and set error_mode_tags to "multi-page,header-noise".
- For low-OCR confidence, add a column "ocr_confidence" with a rough value so we can stratify.

Drive folder with templates and a sample CSV: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-optidocs-prompt-samples

I’ll attach a redaction_checklist_templates.docx to the thread after Naomi confirms.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: OptiDocs discovery recap + request: prompt samples and edge cases

Great — thanks everyone. Sara: can you confirm whether you prefer instruction-only prompts or instruction+examples by EOD today? If you do instruction+examples, please keep example count to <= 3 per prompt to keep the eval consistent.

Next steps from our side (what you'll receive):
- Redaction checklist + CSV template (attachments: redaction_checklist_templates.docx)
- Quick benchmark report with 3 model candidates (Redwood-Prod-7B, Redwood-Large-13B, Redwood-Turbo-3B) within 3 business days after we receive your CSV. Report will include per-field F1, 95p latency, and estimated per-doc cost at your expected volume.
- Suggested rollout: start classification route on Redwood-Turbo-3B, run extraction eval on Prod-7B and Large-13B; if you need stricter accuracy for low-quality OCR, we’ll recommend Private deployment options.

If that all looks good, we’ll treat Thursday EOD as the sample cutoff and kick off the run.

Thanks — talk soon.
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
